recipient: Mr. & Mrs. L. McClelland, 29 Jackson Ave., Jersey City, NJ
notes: Postmarked Warwick, NY, AUG 1, 4:30 PM 1941. “For Defense” Industry Agriculture 1¢ green stamp — a WWII defense-era stamp issued 1940–41. Fotocolor — Made by Dexter Press, Pearl River, NY. Card: Landscape No. 26. Color lithograph of serene Greenwood Lake, NJ — tree-framed lake with mountain and beach. Caption: “Greetings From Greenwood Lake, N.J.” Message: “Hello Folks, Sure are having terrible weather. John is all crippled up in his back. Hope you folks are nearly settled at your place. Love, John & Irene.” McClelland family — same family also received Card #166 (Nashville, 1987).

recipient: Familie Albert Huerske, Houston, 504 Ave of Oaks, Texas, U.S.A.
notes: Written date 7.7.3 (July 7, 2003). No stamp — stamp box empty. Published by Hans Verlag / Hadres Verlag, Hamburg. Card B 285 | 2001-M. Front: stunning black and white multi-view card of Bonn am Rhein showing 7 panels: Rheinpartie (Rhine riverbank), Münster (Bonn Minster cathedral), Rheinterrasse und Rheinbrücke (Rhine terrace and bridge), Münsterplatz und Münster, Bundeshaus (West German Federal Parliament), Beethovenhaus (Beethoven’s birthplace), Villa Hammerschmidt (German presidential residence). Message (translated from German): “My dears! We were with the Pomeranian regional association in Bonn on 7.7. and thought of you. We saw the assembly hall of the Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) where Kennedy once was. We enjoyed it very much. Warm greetings, Betti & Wilhelm. Dear [Hildegard?] and all — your thoughts are always with us with the best wishes. And now we are going to [Leipzig?] to see [?] Trommler for a performance — it was an event of great significance.” Note: JFK visited Bonn in June 1963 and addressed the Bundestag.
